solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grey coat, out of place in class

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are not where they belong, so the two words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grey coat stands out as wrongly worn among the other pupils in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like a school setting but is the definition, in its sense of a group or kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a group of things sharing characteristics, the same as a class or type.

clue.text: Becomes the winner, reportedly, in children's game

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: someone who conquers wins and so becomes the victor

explanation.surface: A child emerges triumphant in a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a traditional British game in which children swing horse chestnuts on strings to smash an opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: Conkers is a playground pastime played with horse chestnuts threaded on string.

clue.text: Story involving British item of furniture

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the story word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale about a piece of British-made furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a common piece of furniture with a flat top on legs.

clue.text: Health's going, suffering in disputed ME territory

indicators.note: suffering suggests being in a bad way or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's health declines as they suffer from ME, the fatigue illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ME' looks like the illness myalgic encephalomyelitis, but here stands for Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golan Heights is a plateau captured by Israel from Syria in 1967, its sovereignty still contested.

clue.text: Royal domain in actual miles

parts.note: real means actual or genuine

explanation.surface: A kingdom whose size is measured in true miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Having little or no rain in Kalahari Desert

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the letters of the next two words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A description of the dry climate of the southern African desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is parched, receiving too little rainfall to support much growth.

clue.text: Article misrepresented performance

indicators.note: something misrepresented is presented wrongly, so the letters are given in a different order

explanation.surface: A newspaper article gave a false account of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetry performance, usually by one player or a small group.

clue.text: Went out, being no longer fashionable

definitions.meaning: to have ... someone is to have gone out with them

explanation.surface: Someone went out on the town looking out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of courting someone and an adjective for outmoded things.

clue.text: Head pupil at Eton, say, may get a pantomime role

parts.note: a principal is the head of a school or college
Eton is a boys' school, so its pupils are boys

explanation.surface: The top pupil at Eton might be cast in the Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, a family Christmas stage show, the principal boy is the young male hero, traditionally played by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal boy is the leading male part in a pantomime, such as Aladdin or Dick Whittington.

clue.text: Philanthropic scientist in Brazil's capital during Christmas

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another, so the letter sits inside the festive word

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, capital letter, here of Brazil's

explanation.surface: A generous scientist visits the Brazilian capital over the Christmas holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests Brasilia, but it means only the initial letter of Brazil's.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, chemist and inventor of dynamite, left his fortune to fund the Nobel Prizes.

clue.text: Mixture of mostly tropical fruit

indicators.note: a mixture jumbles its ingredients together, so the remaining letters are to be rearranged
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A blend made largely of fruit from the tropics, like a smoothie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TROPICAL to TROPICA, and 'Mixture of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, a close relative of the peach and plum.

clue.text: Sheep in wood, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word we want is pronounced like another one

parts.note: yew is a tree and its timber, a type of wood

explanation.surface: A sheep is wandering among the trees, judging by the noise it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, so it is one example of the animal.

clue.text: Exercised control, with name for duke proposed

indicators.note: with one thing for another means it replaces it, so the name letter takes the duke letter's place

parts.note: to dominate is to exercise control over others

explanation.surface: A powerful duke was put forward for office after ruling the roost.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first letter of DOMINATED from D to N.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominated candidate has been put forward, or proposed, for a role or award.

clue.text: Put on leg pad, ultimately

parts.note: a leg of a journey or race is one stage of it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so we take only the last letter of pad

explanation.surface: An instruction for a cricketer to strap on a leg pad at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' looks like dressing, but it is the theatrical sense of mounting a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a play is to stage it, presenting it to an audience.

clue.text: What can make salt last?

parts.note: it reads as preserving salt for longer, but the letters of salt rearranged give last, which is what this wordplay device does

explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like the verb endure, but it is simply the word formed by rearranging the letters of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Reordering a word's letters into another word, as salt into last, is exactly this kind of word puzzle.

clue.text: Lift boy picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the name is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: Philip is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad gets collected and given a ride, or hoisted into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a car ride, but it means a boost to spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost, something that gives a lift to morale.

clue.text: Soldier, in consequence, left umbrella

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
so means therefore, in consequence

explanation.surface: A soldier left his umbrella behind as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella used as shade from the sun.

clue.text: Has girl confused about an imaginary paradise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the short word an
confused letters are muddled, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl is muddled over some dreamt-up idyllic place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges HAS GIRL into SHGRILA, and 'about' wraps that round AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the hidden utopian valley in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, now a byword for an earthly paradise.

clue.text: Frightful bores, sedate and rational

indicators.note: frightful suggests something awful or in a mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Dreadful bores are calm and sensible types.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sober means being serious and level-headed, as well as calm and clear-thinking.

clue.text: Furious judge after one

indicators.note: after places the judge word following the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: A judge is angry at the person in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, which is the same as furious.

clue.text: Daughter must leave expensive organ

indicators.note: must leave says this letter has to go, taken out of the word

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive

explanation.surface: A daughter has to give up an expensive musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the sense organ of hearing.

clue.text: Delete part of chapter, as expected

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor cuts some of a chapter, just as anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to rub it out or delete it.

clue.text: A bitter drunk — it may go to a cardinal's head

definitions.text: it may go to a cardinal's head

indicators.note: a drunk person is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A bitter beer, once drunk, might go to a churchman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to one's head' is said of alcohol, but here the hat literally sits on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, scarlet for cardinals.

clue.text: Supporter with two sons gives money

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports
S is the abbreviation for son, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: A backer with two boys of his own hands over cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for money, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Peculiar piano seat

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: An odd-looking stool for sitting at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suggests a piano stool, but it means the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the buttocks, which in informal use is called the seat.

clue.text: In excellent health all right

definitions.meaning: a reluctant phrase of agreement, as in okay then

explanation.surface: Someone reports that they are fit and fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a description of good health and as a grudging yes, like fine then.
